findings.title: Opening the "/" list on the New task page loops: the panel element changes on every page render and each change re-renders the page
findings.body:
The comment at 240-241 says the panel must be the same element while nothing changes, because the page holds it in state, "so a new one each render would loop". It does not hold on the real page.

`app/spawn.tsx:1094` passes `onChangePrompt={edited(setPrompt)}`. `edited` (spawn.tsx:728) returns a new function on every render of `SpawnPage`. That new function reaches `useSkillSuggestions`, so `select` (the `useCallback` at 228-239, deps `[onChangePrompt]`) is new every render. The `panel` `useMemo` at 242 lists `select` as a dep, so while `show` is true it also returns a new element every render. The effect at spawn-composer.tsx:100 then calls `overlayHost(...)`, which is `setSuggestionOverlay` (spawn.tsx:705). That stores a new object, so `SpawnPage` re-renders, `edited(setPrompt)` is new again, and the cycle repeats.

Once the user types `/` with focus in the field, the page re-renders in a loop. React either aborts with a "Maximum update depth exceeded" error or the app spins on the JS thread.

The tests miss it. They pass a stable `onChangePrompt` (a `vi.fn()` or the `baseProps` default) and a stub host that does not set state, so nothing re-renders.

Fix: read `onChangePrompt` through a ref inside `select`, for example `const latestChange = useRef(onChangePrompt); latestChange.current = onChangePrompt;`, and give `select` empty deps. `latest.current` is already read the same way. Add a test that mounts the composer under a host that sets state in a parent whose `onChangePrompt` is a new function each render.

findings.title: Two comments run together above the overlay state
findings.body: The block at 701-704 starts as a description of `loadSkills` ("The \"/\" list's skills, read from the machine when it opens ... A Cloud task's agent runs in its sandbox"). Its last line, "The open \"/\" list, drawn over the page above the composer", describes `suggestionOverlay`. The result reads as one comment about the wrong declaration. Split it: put the overlay line above `useState`, and the skills/Cloud explanation above `loadSkills` at line 709.
